blocks.content: Every High Court shall have superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.

rows: Remedial constitutional jurisdiction to issue writs
Enforcement of Fundamental Rights and other legal rights
Superintendence over subordinate courts and tribunals
Usually invoked by an aggrieved party's petition
Can be exercised suo motu by the High Court
Does not explicitly exclude military courts from writ scope
Explicitly excludes courts and tribunals of the Armed Forces

items: Article 227 covers both administrative AND judicial superintendence, whereas Article 226 primarily covers writ jurisdiction.
Military courts/tribunals operating under Armed Forces laws are exempt from High Court superintendence under Article 227.
The supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 is extraordinary and used sparingly to keep subordinate courts within their legal bounds.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 227 vests every High Court with the power of superintendence over all subordinate courts and tribunals within its territorial jurisdiction.
The superintendence conferred on the High Court covers both administrative superintendence and judicial superintendence.
The High Court can call for returns, make general rules, and prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of subordinate courts.
Courts and tribunals constituted under any law relating to the Armed Forces (military courts) are strictly excluded from Article 227.
Supervisory power under Article 227 can be exercised by the High Court suo motu (on its own motion).
